body.statement: Can the response-tube handle be completed into priors \(\Pi_n\), independent of the chosen assignment law, such that uniformly over every allocation-count vector \(r\), including every zero-count face, \[\operatorname{BR}_{\Pi_n}(r)\ge n^{-1}-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}-o(n^{-4/3}),\] with a remainder uniform over local counts, positive exterior counts, inactive-arm allocations, and missing-active-arm faces? The proof must establish exact posterior regression for the random finite-population target, weak integration by parts across all response-tube sign cells, and remainder bounds that remain valid after averaging over any dependent outcome-independent design and any randomized labeled-data estimator.
body.justification: This is the genuine open proof boundary: it is the only step that excludes every dependent design at the sharp coefficient.
body.gap: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026), Theorem 2.2 and Appendix B, use a scalar ancillary transform; Hull (2026), Theorem 1, reduces a two-arm finite game but supplies no multi-arm all-face Airy prior.
body.consumer: The inequality certifies that contrast-weighted independent assignment is second-order optimal among all outcome-independent randomizations.
